claim_text: Antimony was detected in 12 of 24 wet-wipe nonwoven sheets, from 187.86 to 19,558.35 µg/L in the digest solution. The highest result is the rayon-only infant sheet (code ML). These figures are not milligrams per kilogram.
quote_trace: Table 5, unit µg/L; ML Sb 19,558.35±3,537.3, fiber Rayon. Abstract range 187.86±5.24 to 19,558.35±3,537.30 µg/L on 12 wet wipes.

claim_text: Nickel was detected in 2 of 24 wet-wipe sheets: 261.26±5.14 µg/L (rayon+polyester+cotton, infant) and 1,242.63±43.71 µg/L (United States, cloth-like). The other 22 sheets were not detected. Units are digest solution, not mg/kg.
quote_trace: Table 5 codes MO and PA*. Ni LOD 0.11 µg/L and LOQ 0.33 µg/L in Table 4.

claim_text: Cadmium, mercury, and thallium were not detected in any of the 24 wet-wipe sheets. Mercury was measured on a separate analyzer. The mercury quantification limit is 0.80 µg/L in Table 4 and 0.08 µg/L in the methods paragraph.
quote_trace: Table 5 dashes for Cd, Hg, and Tl on every wet-wipe row. Table 4 Hg LOQ 0.80. Methods: LOQ on arsenic, mercury and nickel is 007, 0.08, and 0.33 µg/L.

claim_text: A milligrams-per-kilogram reconstruction of the Choi digest was calculated and not adopted as the paper's result. The methods say the sample was diluted with 25 mL of water, not made up to 25 mL. If V is taken as 25 mL and mass as 0.200 g, mg/kg = C(µg/L) × 0.125. Code ML, rayon only, 19,558.35 µg/L, reconstructs to 2,444.79 mg/kg. If the 8 mL of acid is kept and 25 mL of water is added, the factor is 0.165 and the same sheet is 3,227.13 mg/kg. Mercury was not digested.
quote_trace: Section 2.2: Approximately 0.2 g of sample was added into a PTFE vessel containing 7 mL of 70% HNO3 and 1 mL of 50% HF. The samples were then transferred and diluted with 25 mL of ASTM type 1 water. Table 5 ML Sb 19,558.35 µg/L, fiber Rayon.

claim_text: Four consumer-commissioned single-unit ICP-MS reports on zinc oxide diaper creams (40%, 40%, 40% and 13% zinc oxide) found total lead of 3303.8, 1401.0, 4657.1 and 1244.1 ppb and total cadmium of 55.50, 509.5, 473.1 and 45.26 ppb as received. Arsenic was below 10.00 ppb and mercury below 5.00 ppb in all four. Each figure is one unit from one lot, with no published quality control. The evidence is C-tier.
quote_trace: Laboratory report tables: case 2507151 Pb 3303.8, Cd 55.50; case 2508194 Pb 1401.0, Cd 509.5; case 2508207 Pb 4657.1, Cd 473.1; case 2509614 Pb 1244.1, Cd 45.26; As < 10.00; Hg < 5.00 (ppb, ICP-MS, samples as received). Ledger DCL-0001 to DCL-0016.

claim_text: An eleven-product consumer-advocacy chart gives rounded lead of 136 to 4,657 ppb and cadmium of 14.1 to 510 ppb. Four of the eleven values match laboratory reports in this collection. The other seven have no report in the collection and are not verified. For five of those seven products the page does not state whether zinc oxide is present.

claim_text: Zinc from zinc oxide dressings reached the epidermis of intact adult forearm skin: 49 ± 5 µg/g dry weight under a 6% hydrocolloid and 127 ± 26 µg/g under a 25% gum-rosin dressing after 48 h (n=5). In rats with full-thickness wounds, serum zinc rose from 0.95 ± 0.02 µg/ml (control) to 4.06 ± 0.48 and 2.56 ± 0.20 µg/ml after 24 h (n=5 per group). The vehicle changed zinc delivery in opposite directions on intact and wounded skin.
quote_trace: Table I epidermis 49±5 vs 127±26* µg/g dry weight; Table II serum 0.95±0.02, 4.06±0.48***, 2.56±0.20*** µg/ml; liver 146±2, 390±23, 206±11 µg/g dry weight. SEM of 127 recomputes to 22.9 (flag F23).

claim_text: After 48 h of 2 mg/cm2 of a 20% zinc-67 zinc oxide nanoparticle formulation on excised adult human skin, exogenous zinc in viable epidermis was 3.1 ± 0.8 µg/g dry tissue (1.0 ± 0.3 µg/mL by the authors' 70% water conversion), against endogenous 13 ± 2 µg/g (4.3 ± 0.7 µg/mL). The keratinocyte IC50 was 26 ± 5 µg Zn/mL. Particles stayed in the stratum corneum.
quote_trace: Table 1 (VE row) and IC50 26 ± 5 µg Zn/mL; conversion to µg/mL assuming ca. 70% water (p.9; Supplementary S3 not obtained).

claim_text: In one preterm infant (27 weeks 1 day, 542 g) on oral zinc acetate 2 mg/kg/d, serum zinc was 54 µg/dL on day 77. Zinc oxide ointment was started on day 86 for diaper dermatitis that became eroded. Serum zinc was 427 µg/dL on day 93 and 199 µg/dL on day 105, then 52 µg/dL on day 114 after both zinc products were stopped. It was 101 µg/dL on day 128 after oral zinc was restarted on day 116. The authors score the reaction as definite (Naranjo 9).
quote_trace: Fig. 1 and case text; restart day 116 per Japanese text and Fig. 1, abstract says 114 (flag F28).

claim_text: The EU SCCS opinion on nano zinc oxide states that no information was provided on impurities or contaminants. From purity of 99% or more it infers impurities of 1% or less, and it gives no lead, cadmium, arsenic or mercury figure. It adopts 0.03% of the applied dose as the dermally absorbed fraction of zinc.
quote_trace: Section 3.1.5: No information has been provided on the presence of impurities/contaminants ... impurities/contaminants are ≤1%. Section 3.3.4.1: SCCS considers that 0.03% of the applied dose may be absorbed.

claim_text: ICH Q3D(R2) Appendix 5 gives cutaneous permitted daily exposures for drug products of cadmium 20, lead 50, arsenic 30 and mercury 30 µg/day, nickel 200 µg/day with a 35 µg/g concentration limit, and chromium 11000 µg/day. For a 10 g daily dose these equal cadmium 2, lead 5, arsenic 3 and mercury 3 µg/g. The generic cutaneous PDE is not to be applied to skin with substantial disruption of the basal cell layer, for which the parenteral PDE is the starting point.

claim_text: 21 CFR 73.1991 (2025) requires zinc oxide used as a colour additive in externally applied drugs to contain at least 99% zinc oxide and not more than 15 ppm cadmium, 1 ppm mercury, 3 ppm arsenic and 20 ppm lead. §73.2991 applies the same specifications to zinc oxide colour in cosmetics. These are ingredient specifications, not finished-product limits, and do not govern zinc oxide used as a skin-protectant active.
